statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If every instance of the received Configuration Options is recognizable, but some values are not acceptable, then the implementation MUST transmit a Configure-Nak.
statements.trigger: Configure-Request received with all options recognizable but some values unacceptable

statements.subject: message
statements.description: All acceptable Configuration Options are filtered out of the Configure-Nak, but otherwise the Configuration Options from the Configure-Request MUST NOT be reordered.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Options which have no value fields (boolean options) MUST use the Configure-Reject reply instead.
statements.trigger: Configure-Request received containing option with no value fields
actions: send Configure-Reject instead of Configure-Nak for boolean options

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Each Configuration Option which is allowed only a single instance MUST be modified to a value acceptable to the Configure-Nak sender.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The default value MAY be used, when this differs from the requested value.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When a particular type of Configuration Option can be listed more than once with different values, the Configure-Nak MUST include a list of all values for that option which are acceptable to the Configure-Nak sender.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If that option is not listed, then that option MAY be appended to the list of Nak'd Configuration Options, in order to prompt the peer to include that option in its next Configure-Request packet.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any value fields for the option MUST indicate values acceptable to the Configure-Nak sender.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Nak, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request.
actions: validate that Configure-Nak Identifier matches last transmitted Configure-Request Identifier
silently discard packet if Identifier does not match

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Reception of a valid Configure-Nak indicates that when a new Configure-Request is sent, the Configuration Options MAY be modified as specified in the Configure-Nak.
actions: optionally modify Configuration Options for next Configure-Request as specified in Configure-Nak

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: When multiple instances of a Configuration Option are present, the peer SHOULD select a single value to include in its next Configure-Request packet.
statements.trigger: valid Configure-Nak received with multiple instances of a Configuration Option
actions: select single value from Configure-Nak option instances for inclusion in next Configure-Request

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Since the Nak'd Option has been modified by the peer, the implementation MUST be able to handle an Option length which is different from the original Configure-Request.
